deities: Lakulisha (founder of the Pashupata sect of Shaivism; principal deity)
Dakshinamurti, Brahma, Vishnu, Indra, Ambika (carved images)

history.summary: The Lakulisha temple is the earliest temple on Pavagadh hill, a 10th-11th-century Solanki-period Shaivite shrine on the Mauliya plateau dedicated to Lakulisha, the founder of the Pashupata sect of Shaivism. It survives only as ruins: the gudha mandapa (sanctum sanctorum) and the ardha mandapa of the antarala are what remain. Built in the Nagara style with garbhagriha, mandapa and entrance porch, it carries ornate stone carvings of Lakulisha, Dakshinamurti, Brahma, Vishnu, Gajendra Moksha, various forms of Shiva, Indra, seated Ambika and Sura-Sundaris. The Structural Temples of Gujarat describes it as standing on a peninsula jutting into a tank, with most of the garbhagriha and shikhara collapsed (the media image matches this description). The lintel over the mandapa entrance bears a figure of Lakulisha, and a Nandi in front confirms its Shaiva character. It is an archaeological monument within the Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site); active worship status unverified — treat as ruins, not a functioning shrine. name: Lakulisha Temple, Pavagadh
town_description: Pavagadh is a hill town in Panchmahal district, Gujarat, dominated by the 800-metre Pavagadh hill — one of India's oldest rock formations. Together with Champaner at its base, it forms the Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where Hindu and Jain temples stand beside medieval Islamic mosques and palaces. The Lakulisha temple stands on the Mauliya plateau, near the mid-hill ropeway station.
